input: How do I perform Medicine Ball Scoop Throw with good form?
response: A plyometric (jumping/explosive) exercise for the shoulders, done using a medicine ball. It also works the abdominals, hamstrings and quadriceps. How to do it: Assume a semisquat stance with a medicine ball in your hands. Your arms should hang so the ball is near your feet. Begin by thrusting the hips forward as you extend through the legs, jumping up. As you do, swing your arms up and over your head, keeping them extended, releasing the ball at the peak of your movement. The goal is to throw the ball the greatest distance behind you. Safety tip: Land softly with knees tracking over the toes, and only add volume once your landings stay quiet and controlled.

Eating within a few hours is sufficient for most people.

instruction: You are FitBot, a fitness assistant.
input: How do I perform Snatch with good form?
response: An Olympic weightlifting movement for the quadriceps, done using a barbell. It also works the biceps, glutes and hamstrings. How to do it: Place your feet at a shoulder width stance with the barbell resting right above the connection between the toes and the rest of the foot. With a palms facing down grip, bend at the knees and keeping the back flat grab the bar using a wider than shoulder width grip. Bring the hips down and make sure that your body drops as if you were going to sit on a chair. This will be your starting position. Safety tip: This is a technical lift - learn it with a coach and an empty bar or PVC pipe before adding weight.

input: Tips for doing the All Fours Quad Stretch safely?
response: A stretch for the quadriceps, done with no equipment. It also works the quadriceps. input: How do I do the Cable Rope Rear-Delt Rows?
response: A strength exercise for the shoulders, done using a cable machine. It also works the biceps and middle back. How to do it: Sit in the same position on a low pulley row station as you would if you were doing seated cable rows for the back. Attach a rope to the pulley and grasp it with an overhand grip. input: Tips for doing the Standing Bent-Over Two-Arm Dumbbell Triceps Extension safely?
response: A strength exercise for the triceps, done with dumbbells. How to do it: With a dumbbell in each hand and the palms facing your torso, bend your knees slightly and bring your torso forward, by bending at the waist, while keeping the back straight until it is almost parallel to the floor. Make sure that you keep the head up. The upper arms should be close to the torso and parallel to the floor while the forearms are pointing towards the floor as the hands hold the weights. Tip: There should be a 90-degree angle between the forearms and the upper arm. This is your starting position. Safety tip: Pick a weight you can control through the full range, and set the dumbbells down carefully rather than dropping them.

instruction: You are FitBot, a fitness assistant.
input: How do I do cable crossover?
response: A cable fly variation that keeps constant tension on the chest throughout the movement. It mainly targets the chest and shoulders. How to do it: To get yourself into the starting position, place the pulleys on a high position (above your head), select the resistance to be used and hold the pulleys in each hand Step forward in front of an imaginary straight line between both pulleys while pulling your arms together in front of you. Safety tip: Stand in a staggered stance for balance and control the return; do not let the cables pull your arms back quickly.

input: How do I perform Chest Push (multiple response) with good form?
response: A plyometric (jumping/explosive) exercise for the chest, done using a medicine ball. It also works the abdominals, shoulders and triceps. How to do it: Begin in a kneeling position facing a wall or utilize a partner. Hold the ball with both hands tight into the chest. Immediately return to an upright position. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions. Safety tip: Land softly with knees tracking over the toes, and only add volume once your landings stay quiet and controlled.

instruction: You are FitBot, a fitness assistant.
input: What's the proper form for Exercise Ball Crunch?
response: A strength exercise for the abdominals, done using an exercise ball. How to do it: Lie on an exercise ball with your lower back curvature pressed against the spherical surface of the ball. Your feet should be bent at the knee and pressed firmly against the floor. The upper torso should be hanging off the top of the ball. The arms should either be kept alongside the body or crossed on top of your chest as these positions avoid neck strains (as opposed to the hands behind the back of the head position). Safety tip: Use a correctly inflated ball on a non-slip surface and start near a wall for balance.

instruction: You are FitBot, a fitness assistant.
input: How do I do the Glute Bridge?
response: A floor exercise that strengthens the glutes and hamstrings with no equipment. How to do it: Lay on the floor with your feet flat and knees bent. Raise one leg off of the ground, pulling the knee to your chest. This will be your starting position. Execute the movement by driving through the heel, extending your hip upward and raising your glutes off of the ground. Extend as far as possible, pause and then return to the starting position. Safety tip: Squeeze your glutes to lift, avoid overarching your lower back; start with both feet down before progressing to one leg.

instruction: You are FitBot, a fitness assistant.
input: How do I perform Kneeling High Pulley Row with good form?
response: A strength exercise for the lats, done using a cable machine. It also works the biceps and middle back. How to do it: Select the appropriate weight using a pulley that is above your head. Attach a rope to the cable and kneel a couple of feet away, holding the rope out in front of you with both arms extended. This will be your starting position. Initiate the movement by flexing the elbows and fully retracting your shoulders, pulling the rope toward your upper chest with your elbows out. After pausing briefly, slowly return to the starting position. Safety tip: Check the pin is fully inserted and the attachment is secure, and control the weight on the way back.
